disclaimer: This is SYNTHETIC data with injected known truth, not real flow-cytometer acquisition data. It must never be presented as, or substituted for, real independently-labelled acquisitions. It calibrates detector behavior against a controlled ground truth, which is a narrower claim than QC-CAL-01's actual ask.

backward_time_jump_run.expected_behavior: The backward move at event index 2700 occurs far below 80% of the (large) Time full-scale, so prepareTimeQCBins should classify it as an unrelated jump and start a new acquisition segment (segmentCount==2), and runTimeQC should report limitedReliability=true purely from segmentCount>1.

injected_disturbance.type: unrelated backward time jump (simulates a paused/restarted acquisition, not a timer wrap)

clog_run.expected_behavior: runTimeQC should flag the bin(s) overlapping event indexes [2400, 3000] via the eventRate metric (and plausibly medianFSC_A/medianSSC_A/medianDNA_A too), producing at least one flaggedInterval overlapping this range.

injected_disturbance.type: localized event-rate slowdown with mild scatter/DNA-A distortion

debris_dominant_run.expected_behavior: CALIBRATION FINDING (confirmed by running the real detector against this corpus, not assumed): gateMainBiologicalCloud selects its 'main' component purely by population weight (see its selectionScore in scatter_gmm_gate.js). With debris at 60% -- a genuine majority -- the debris cluster IS the higher-weight component, so the gate selects it as 'main' and rejects the live-cell cloud instead: most non-debris events are incorrectly flagged (false-positive rate near 1.0) while most true debris events are retained (recall near 0). It also reports 'review required' rather than a clean fit. This is the expected, correct behavior of the documented weight-based selection rule once debris crosses 50% of events -- it is a real operating-envelope limit of QC-05, not a bug in this fixture, and is worth a note in docs/scientific-result-contract.md: gateMainBiologicalCloud is only reliable while the live-cell population is the numeric majority.

injected_disturbance.type: debris cluster outnumbers the live-cell cloud in FSC-A/SSC-A

doublet_heavy_run.expected_behavior: gateByPulseGeometry should flag a majority of the doublet_event_indices events as off-ridge (excess Area relative to Height/at the widened Width). Time QC and the scatter gate should behave as in stable_run -- only the pulse-geometry gate is the intended target. CALIBRATION NOTE (found by running the real detector against this corpus): gateByPulseGeometry's robust ridge fit assumes doublets are a minority of the population (see its own module docstring). Sweeping this fixture's doublet fraction against the real gate shows recall holds near 1.0 up to roughly 8-10% doublets, then degrades progressively as the fraction rises further, and selectPulseGeometry's correlation-based DNA_H/DNA_W channel choice can itself flip to the weaker channel at conflated fractions. DOUBLET_HEAVY_FRACTION is deliberately set inside that still-reliable range so this fixture checks detection, not the breakdown point; the breakdown itself is a real, separate finding worth a scientific-result-contract note, not something this fixture asserts.

injected_disturbance.type: elevated doublet fraction, uniformly distributed across acquisition time

dropout_run.expected_behavior: The bin(s) spanning event index 3300 should show a sharply elongated duration (hence depressed eventRate) relative to the robust baseline and be flagged; no channel-value distortion is injected here, only a timing gap.

injected_disturbance.type: full acquisition gap (no events observed for a span of time)

stable_run.expected_behavior: Negative control / false-positive-rate baseline for all three gates. Time QC should report a single segment with no flagged intervals; the pulse-geometry and scatter gates should retain nearly all events at only the small background doublet/debris rate above.

timer_rollover_run.expected_behavior: This is otherwise a well-behaved constant-rate acquisition -- the ONLY disturbance is the wraps themselves. prepareTimeQCBins should unwrap every wrap into a single continuous segment (segmentCount==1) and runTimeQC should NOT flag elevated bins from the wraps alone. This is a specificity / false-positive-rate check on the wrap-handling branch, not a positive-detection check.

injected_disturbance.type: deliberately small $PnR Time full-scale causing repeated wraps
